name: Rules of Acquisition — each mode keeps its own controller rule
notes: Found by the full audit on the 2026-11-25 card data. Both modes' target lists were empty: _finalizeEffects (cards-parser-post.js) gave every targeted effect any controller rule found on another, so mode 1 ('an opponent controls') and mode 2 ('you control') each had both; and 'Target opponent gains control of target nonland permanent you control' also set the card-wide _youControlRequired, which the single picker reads whichever mode is picked. On a modal spell a controller rule now spreads only within its mode, and the card-wide flag is not set. Mode 1 lists the opponent's Hill Giant and Sol Ring copy only; mode 2 lists your Grizzly Bears and Sol Ring only (never a land).

scryfallData.name: Grizzly Bears
scryfallData.flavor_text:
"We cannot forget that among all of Dominaria's wonders, a system of life exists, with prey and predators that will never fight wars nor vie for ancient power."
—Jolrael, empress of beasts

scryfallData.name: Sol Ring
scryfallData.flavor_text:
"Actually, 'warp core' is a misnomer. It is technically a generator, but it's not a warp field generator. For some reason, 'deuterium/anti-deuterium intermix reactor' never caught on. Funny, right?"
—Lieutenant junior grade Sam Rutherford

scryfallData.name: Forest
scryfallData.flavor_text:
"You have only one mission, minions: protect me with your lives. In order to do this, you need to wear down Captain Britain's psyche. In order to do *that*, you need to burn down her precious lands. Am I understood?"
—Morgan Le Fay

scryfallData.name: Hill Giant
scryfallData.flavor_text: Fortunately, hill giants have large blind spots in which a human can easily hide. Unfortunately, these blind spots are beneath the bottoms of their feet.
